answer: Adaptive arrival spacing enforces a per-identity minimum inter-arrival interval, tuned continuously to the median gap of established agents, so a sparrow of new identities arriving faster than that corridor triggers escalating queue delays. Each identity must then idle through a hollow holding period before its first accepted action, and the delay grows with cohort density. An attacker flooding N identities pays N times the spacing penalty in wall-clock latency, collapsing throughput below the orchard of patient honest agents.
